def-reversed-transition-kernels-for-diff:
## Definition

Let $T>0$, let $p_t$ be a strictly positive probability density on $\mathbb R^d$ for each $t\in[0,T]$, and let $q(s,x;t,y)$ be a jointly Borel, strictly positive transition density for $0\le s<t\le T$. Assume the marginal identity $p_t(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}p_s(x)q(s,x;t,y)\,dx$ and the Chapman–Kolmogorov identity $q(s,x;t,y)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}q(s,x;r,z)q(r,z;t,y)\,dz$ whenever $s<r<t$. For $0\le u<v\le T$ define
$$K_{u,v}(y,A)=\frac{\int_A p_{T-v}(x)q(T-v,x;T-u,y)\,dx}{p_{T-u}(y)}\qquad(A\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ Borel}),$$
and set $K_{u,u}(y,\cdot)=\delta_y$. This is the Bayes-reversed transition probability kernel from reverse time $u$ to reverse time $v$; its source state $y$ is the forward-time state at $T-u$ and its output $x$ is the state at $T-v$.
lem-continuous-local-martingale-quadrati:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a real continuous local martingale on $[0,T]$ with $M_0=0$, where a local martingale means that some increasing stopping times tending to $T$ make the stopped processes martingales. Then there is a unique continuous increasing process $[M]$ with $[M]_0=0$ such that the step-endpoint and partial-increment sums of squared increments along every deterministic partition sequence whose mesh tends to zero converge uniformly in probability to $[M]$. Moreover $M_t^2-[M]_t$ is a continuous local martingale. For a continuous $d$-dimensional local martingale $M$ started at zero, polarization defines continuous covariations $[M^i,M^j]$ with $M^iM^j-[M^i,M^j]$ local martingales. More generally, if $X=M+A$ and $Z=N+C$ with continuous local martingales $M,N$ and continuous finite-variation processes $A,C$, then left-step sums define the localized integrals against $M,N$ and
$$X_tZ_t-X_0Z_0=\int_0^t X_s\,dZ_s+\int_0^t Z_s\,dX_s+[M,N]_t,$$
where finite-variation integrals are pathwise Lebesgue–Stieltjes integrals and local-martingale integrals are the limits of the displayed left-step sums. A continuous finite-variation local martingale is constant.
lem-density-translation-factorization:
## Statement

Let $m,r\ge1$, and let $A\in\mathbb R^m$ and $B,C\in\mathbb R^r$ have a joint Lebesgue density. Suppose this joint density factors as
$$p_{A,B,C}(a,b,c)=p_A(a)f(b-c)p_C(c)$$
almost everywhere, where $p_A$, $f$, and $p_C$ are probability densities on $\mathbb R^m$, $\mathbb R^r$, and $\mathbb R^r$, respectively. Then $D=B-C$ is independent of $A$, has density $f$, and the joint density of $(A,D)$ is $p_A(a)f(d)$.
lem-elliptic-local-martingale-brownian-r:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a continuous adapted $d$-dimensional local martingale with $M_0=0$. Let $(\sigma_t)_{0\le t\le T}$ be a continuous adapted process of invertible $d\times d$ matrices such that $\|\sigma_t^{-1}\|\le C$ for a deterministic finite constant $C$, and suppose every entry of $\sigma$ is locally square-integrable in time almost surely. Write $[M^i,M^j]$ for the continuous bracket characterized by the local-martingale property of $M^iM^j-[M^i,M^j]$, and assume
$$[M^i,M^j]_t=\int_0^t(\sigma_s\sigma_s^{\mathsf T})_{ij}\,ds\qquad(1\le i,j\le d).$$
Then the stochastic integral $B_t=\int_0^t\sigma_s^{-1}\,dM_s$, constructed as the localized $L^2$ limit of left-step sums, has a continuous version with $[B^i,B^j]_t=\delta_{ij}t$. Consequently $B$ is a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion relative to the given filtration.
lem-reversed-kernels-and-generator-ident:
## Statement

Let $X_t$ have continuous paths on $[0,T]$ and be Markov on $\mathbb R^d$, meaning its conditional future law given the past depends only on its current state; nonexplosive means it remains in $\mathbb R^d$ throughout this finite interval. Let it have forward generator
$$L_t\phi=b_t\cdot\nabla\phi+\tfrac12a_t:D^2\phi,$$
where $a_t=\sigma_t\sigma_t^{\mathsf T}$ is symmetric and $L_t^*r=-\partial_i(b_{t,i}r)+\tfrac12\partial_i\partial_j(a_{t,ij}r)$. Assume positive $C^{1,2}$ marginal densities $p_t$ and positive transition densities $q(s,x;t,y)$ satisfy the marginal identity and Chapman–Kolmogorov identity, and that $\partial_t p_t=L_t^*p_t$ and $\partial_tq(s,x;t,y)=L_t^{*,y}q(s,x;t,y)$ hold classically. Assume for every $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ that the transition-density integrals can be differentiated in time, the resulting derivatives are integrable, and integration by parts in the state variable has no boundary term. Define $K_{u,v}$ by the Bayes-reversed kernel formula for $0\le u\le v\le T$. Then the reversed process $Y_u=X_{T-u}$ is Markov with transitions $K_{u,v}$, and for every $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ and $0\le u<T$ its generator is
$$\widetilde L_u\phi(y)=\frac{L_{T-u}^*(p_{T-u}\phi)(y)-\phi(y)L_{T-u}^*p_{T-u}(y)}{p_{T-u}(y)}.$$
It solves the corresponding local martingale problem. Expanding the adjoint product rule gives
$$\widetilde L_u\phi=\widetilde b_u\cdot\nabla\phi+\tfrac12a_{T-u}:D^2\phi,\qquad \widetilde b_u=-b_{T-u}+\nabla\!\cdot a_{T-u}+a_{T-u}\nabla\log p_{T-u},$$
with $(\nabla\!\cdot a)_i=\sum_j\partial_j a_{ij}$.
thm-anderson-reverse-time-diffusion:
## Statement

Assume AC. Fix $t_0<T$, integers $d,r\ge1$, and a filtered probability space carrying a standard $r$-dimensional Brownian motion $W$. Let
$$dX_t=b(X_t,t)\,dt+\sigma(X_t,t)\,dW_t,\qquad X_t\in\mathbb R^d,$$
Assume this SDE has a unique nonexplosive strong solution, $X_{t_0}$ is almost surely bounded and independent of the Brownian process, and $a=\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T}$. Assume the coefficients and densities are smooth enough for the displayed derivatives and Itô identities to hold. Assume the marginal density $p_t(x)$ is positive wherever used and is a unique smooth solution of
$$\partial_t p_t=L_t^*p_t,\qquad L_t^*r=-\sum_i\partial_i(b_i r)+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\partial_i\partial_j(a_{ij}r).$$
Define the $r$-vector process $\widetilde W$ by $\widetilde W_{t_0}=0$ and
$$d\widetilde W_t^k=dW_t^k+c_k(X_t,t)\,dt,\qquad c_k(x,t)=p_t(x)^{-1}\sum_i\partial_i\!\left(p_t(x)\sigma_{ik}(x,t)\right).$$
Assume the augmented process $(X,\widetilde W)$ has a unique smooth joint density solving its augmented forward Kolmogorov equation for $t>t_0$, and for every $t>s\ge t_0$ its conditional joint density given $\widetilde W_s$ is the unique smooth solution of the corresponding conditional augmented equation; all displayed derivatives and density integrals are valid. Then the following hold.

1. For $t>s\ge t_0$, $X_t$ is independent of $\widetilde W_t-\widetilde W_s$, and this increment has law $N_r(0,(t-s)I_r)$.
2. Put $U=T-t_0$, $Y_u=X_{T-u}$, and $B_u=\widetilde W_{T-u}-\widetilde W_T$ for $0\le u\le U$. With $\mathcal G_u=\sigma(Y_v,B_v:0\le v\le u)$, $B$ is a standard $r$-dimensional Brownian motion relative to $(\mathcal G_u)$.
3. In the backward Itô convention, $Y$ satisfies
$$dY_u=\left[-b(Y_u,T-u)+(\nabla\!\cdot a)(Y_u,T-u)+a(Y_u,T-u)\nabla\log p_{T-u}(Y_u)\right]du+\sigma(Y_u,T-u)\,dB_u,$$
where $(\nabla\!\cdot a)_i=\sum_j\partial_j a_{ij}$. The score is asserted only where $p_{T-u}>0$; no density or score regularity beyond the stated hypotheses is implied.
def-bayes-reversed-gaussian-smoothing-ke:
## Definition

Assume AC. Fix $T>0$, a compactly supported Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^d$, a continuously differentiable function $g:[0,T]\to(0,\infty)$ bounded above and away from zero, and $v(t)=\int_0^t g(r)^2dr$. For $t>0$ put
$$p_t(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_{v(t)}(y-z)\,\mu(dz),\qquad q(s,x;t,y)=\phi_{v(t)-v(s)}(y-x)\quad(0\le s<t\le T),$$
where $\phi_a$ is the centered Gaussian density with covariance $aI_d$. Put $p_0=\mu$ as a probability measure, not as a Lebesgue density. For $0\le u<v<T$ define
$$K_{u,v}(y,dx)=\frac{p_{T-v}(x)q(T-v,x;T-u,y)}{p_{T-u}(y)}\,dx,$$
and for $0\le u<T$ at the singular data endpoint define
$$K_{u,T}(y,A)=\frac{\int_A q(0,x;T-u,y)\,\mu(dx)}{p_{T-u}(y)}\quad(A\text{ Borel}).$$
Set $K_{u,u}(y,\cdot)=\delta_y$. These are the Bayes-reversed kernels of the additive Gaussian smoothing process, including the posterior kernel at the original data time; no density for $\mu$ is required.
thm-markov-diffusion-reversal-by-bayes-k:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a continuous nonexplosive Markov diffusion on $[0,T]$ in $\mathbb R^d$, where nonexplosive means its paths remain in $\mathbb R^d$ throughout the interval and Markov means conditional future laws given the past depend only on the current state. It satisfies
$$dX_t=b_t(X_t)dt+\sigma_t(X_t)dW_t,$$
where $W$ is standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion and $\sigma_t(x)$ is square and invertible with $\sup_{t,x}\|\sigma_t(x)^{-1}\|<\infty$. Put $a_t(x)=\sigma_t(x)\sigma_t(x)^{\mathsf T}$. A transition density means $P(X_t\in dy\mid X_s=x)=q(s,x;t,y)dy$. Assume $p_t$ and $q(s,x;t,y)$ are positive probability densities, with $p_t$ having one continuous time derivative and two continuous state derivatives, and satisfying
$$p_t(y)=\int p_s(x)q(s,x;t,y)dx,\qquad q(s,x;t,y)=\int q(s,x;r,z)q(r,z;t,y)dz\quad(s<r<t).$$
For $L_t\phi=b_t\cdot\nabla\phi+\tfrac12a_t:D^2\phi$, define its formal adjoint by $L_t^*r=-\partial_i(b_{t,i}r)+\tfrac12\partial_i\partial_j(a_{t,ij}r)$ and assume $\partial_t p_t=L_t^*p_t$ and $\partial_tq(s,x;t,y)=L_t^{*,y}q(s,x;t,y)$ classically. Assume that for every compactly supported smooth test function the transition integrals and their time derivatives are absolutely integrable, differentiation under those integrals is valid, and integration by parts in space has no boundary term. For each initial law, assume the reverse martingale problem for the operator defined by the Bayes-density expression below has a unique nonexplosive continuous solution in law; here this means existence and uniqueness in law of a continuous process for which each compact-test compensated process is a local martingale.

For $0\le u<v\le T$ define
$$K_{u,v}(y,dx)=\frac{p_{T-v}(x)q(T-v,x;T-u,y)}{p_{T-u}(y)}\,dx,$$
and let $Y_u=X_{T-u}$ with reversed filtration $\mathcal G_u=\sigma(Y_r:0\le r\le u)$. Then these are the transition kernels of $Y$, and for $0\le u<T$ its generator on $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ is
$$\widetilde L_u\phi=p_{T-u}^{-1}\{L_{T-u}^*(p_{T-u}\phi)-\phi L_{T-u}^*p_{T-u}\}.$$
Consequently $Y$ solves the reverse SDE
$$dY_u=\left[-b_{T-u}(Y_u)+(\nabla\!\cdot a_{T-u})(Y_u)+a_{T-u}(Y_u)\nabla\log p_{T-u}(Y_u)\right]du+\sigma_{T-u}(Y_u)dB_u,$$
where $(\nabla\!\cdot a)_i=\sum_j\partial_j a_{ij}$ and $B$ is a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion in the reversed filtration. This theorem starts from the assumed positive density regime; it does not infer densities from strong SDE well-posedness.
lem-reversed-smoothing-generator-and-mar:
## Statement

Assume AC and the compactly supported Gaussian smoothing setup: $X_t=X_0+\int_0^t g(r)dW_r$, with $X_0\sim\mu$ compactly supported, scalar $g\in C^1([0,T])$ bounded above and away from zero, $v(t)=\int_0^t g(r)^2dr$, $p_t(x)=\int\phi_{v(t)}(x-z)\mu(dz)$ for $t>0$, and forward transition density $q(s,x;t,y)=\phi_{v(t)-v(s)}(y-x)$. Fix $0<\epsilon<T$, put $Y_u=X_{T-u}$ for $0\le u\le T-\epsilon$, and use the Bayes-reversed kernels from the preceding definition. For $s_t=\nabla\log p_t$, define
$$\widetilde L_u\varphi(y)=g(T-u)^2\left(s_{T-u}(y)\cdot\nabla\varphi(y)+\tfrac12\Delta\varphi(y)\right),\qquad \varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d).$$
Then $Y$ is Markov with those reversed kernels, and for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty$ the process
$$\varphi(Y_v)-\varphi(Y_0)-\int_0^v\widetilde L_r\varphi(Y_r)\,dr,\qquad 0\le v\le T-\epsilon,$$
is a martingale in the natural reversed filtration. The assertion is restricted to forward times at least $\epsilon$; it makes no score or density claim at $t=0$.
thm-gaussian-smoothing-reversal-on-trunc:
## Statement

Assume AC. Fix $d\ge1$, $T>0$, a Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported in $\overline B(0,R)$ for a finite $R$, and $g\in C^1([0,T])$ with $0<g_{\min}\le g(t)\le g_{\max}<\infty$. Let $W$ be standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion with increments independent of the past, let $X_0\sim\mu$ be independent of future Brownian increments, and set
$$X_t=X_0+\int_0^t g(r)dW_r,\qquad v(t)=\int_0^t g(r)^2dr,\qquad p_t(x)=\int\phi_{v(t)}(x-z)\mu(dz)\quad(t>0).$$
For $0<\epsilon<T$, set $Y_u=X_{T-u}$ on $0\le u\le T-\epsilon$. Then there is a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion $B$ in the usual augmentation of the natural reversed filtration such that
$$dY_u=g(T-u)^2\nabla\log p_{T-u}(Y_u)\,du+g(T-u)\,dB_u,\qquad 0\le u<T-\epsilon.$$
The reverse drift is globally Lipschitz in the state on this truncated interval, with constant at most $g_{\max}^2(1/v(\epsilon)+R^2/v(\epsilon)^2)$ when $\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq\overline B(0,R)$, and has linear growth. The endpoint coupling satisfies
$$\mathbb E|Y_{T-\epsilon}-X_0|^2=dv(\epsilon),\qquad W_2(\operatorname{Law}(Y_{T-\epsilon}),\mu)\le\sqrt{dv(\epsilon)},$$
where $W_2$ is the infimum of root mean-square cost over probability couplings with finite second moments. Consequently $Y_{T-\epsilon}=X_\epsilon$ converges to $X_0$ in $L^2$ and its law converges weakly to $\mu$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. No score or density regularity at $t=0$ is asserted.
